name: Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises
summary: Mandates that Central Government Ministries, Departments and CPSEs source a minimum 25% of their annual procurement value from Micro and Small Enterprises, with sub-targets reserved for SC/ST and women-owned MSEs.
administering_ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
benefit_description: Preferential access to Central Government procurement: 25% of total annual procurement is reserved for MSEs, with 4% sub-reserved for SC/ST-owned MSEs and 3% sub-reserved for women-owned MSEs.

criteria.description: Enterprise must hold a valid Udyam Registration to be classified as a Micro or Small Enterprise for procurement preference purposes.
criteria.source_quote: Under amended Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, Order 2012 a minimum 25 per cent share out of the total annual procurement by Central Government Ministries / Departments / Public Sector Undertakings are to be made from MSEs.

criteria.description: For the SC/ST sub-target (4%) or women sub-target (3%) within the 25% reservation, the enterprise must be majority-owned by the relevant category and register on the Government e-Marketplace or with NSIC accordingly.
criteria.source_quote: out of 25% target of annual procurement from MSEs (Not in the specific tender), a sub-target of 4% (within the 25%) of annual procurement from MSEs is earmarked for procurement from MSEs owned by Scheduled Caste (SC) / Scheduled Tribe (ST) entrepreneurs and 3% (within the 25%) of annual procurement from MSEs is earmarked for procurement from MSEs owned by women entrepreneur.

document_requirements.how_to_obtain: Register on the national Udyam portal.
Register as a seller on the Government e-Marketplace and/or with NSIC to be discoverable by procuring ministries.

document_requirements.document_name: Caste/ownership proof (if claiming SC/ST or women sub-target)
document_requirements.how_to_obtain: Obtain caste certificate or ownership proof establishing majority SC/ST or women ownership, if claiming the reserved sub-target.

windows.notes: Standing policy, not a time-bound application window; procurement preference applies to every eligible government tender.

benefits.description: Priority access to a mandated share of Central Government procurement value.
benefits.conditions_for_disbursement: Not a cash disbursement; benefit is realised through winning reserved-category tenders and purchase orders.
benefits.source_quote: Overall procurement goal of minimum 25% has become mandatory from 1st April 2015.
